To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a Bayesian analysis of logistic regression can be performed using penalized maximum likelihood estimation via data-augmentation; and (ii) a command has been developed to perform such analysis, which allows one to assess information content of priors in terms of the equivalent data.

(a) the penlogit command can be used to estimate the parameters of a logistic model using penalized likelihood via data augmentation; (b) this command automatically adds specific data records to a dataset that are computed to generate a penalty function that is equivalent to a prior on the model parameters; (c) this command overcomes the need for specialized software to fit Bayesian models, and provides a way to translate background information into prior-data records, allowing calculation of approximate posterior summaries using maximum likelihood estimation;

the use of penalized likelihood via data augmentation allows one to fit a Bayesian model with any prior distribution that is a function of a linear combination of the data, and that it allows the use of ordinary maximum likelihood programs to obtain approximate posterior distributions for Bayesian models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new command for approximate Bayesian logistic models, which allows one to assess prior information in terms of the amount of data that it is equivalent to.
the use of penalized likelihood estimation for Bayesian logistic regression.

developing and applying a Bayesian approach to modeling and inference for the analysis of observational data, with the aim of providing an approach to the analysis of such data that can be implemented using standard statistical software and that is flexible and robust to model specification.

, by adding a small number of prior-data records to an existing dataset, one can fit a Bayesian model without the need for specialized software or tools.
